 "decisions": [
  {
   "id": "ADR-1",
   "title": "Harden SQLite with a connect listener, connect_args timeout and QueuePool settings",
   "decision": "For file-based SQLite:\n- create_engine(url, poolclass=QueuePool, pool_size, max_overflow, pool_timeout, connect_args={'check_same_thread': False, 'timeout': (SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS + 0.5) / 1000.0}).\n- An event.listens_for(engine, 'connect') handler executes the literal statements 'PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL' and 'PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL' on a raw DBAPI cursor.\n- The +0.5 ms makes pysqlite's int(timeout*1000) truncation land exactly on the configured value.\n\nIn-memory SQLite gets only check_same_thread=False. Non-SQLite gets pool_pre_ping=True plus the pool settings.",
   "rationale": "WAL lets readers proceed while a writer holds the lock, which is what stops redirects queueing behind creates and clicks. The sqlite3 timeout parameter installs the busy handler without building a PRAGMA string, so the literal-only SQL policy holds. QueuePool kwargs are not valid for SingletonThreadPool/StaticPool, so in-memory URLs skip them.",
   "alternatives": [
    "PRAGMA busy_timeout=<n> built with formatting (violates policy)",
    "Move to PostgreSQL now (rejected by Q-2; needs a driver)",
    "Leave the rollback journal and only add a busy timeout (readers would still block)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "id": "ADR-2",
   "title": "Idempotent startup ALTER instead of migration tooling",
   "decision": "After create_all, the lifespan calls app.core.schema.ensure_links_expires_at(engine):\n- It uses sqlalchemy.inspect on a fresh connection.\n- If 'expires_at' is not among the links columns, it runs the dialect-guarded literal ALTER inside engine.begin().\n- It logs 'added' or 'already_present'.\n- On any exception it logs an ERROR and re-raises, so startup aborts.",
   "rationale": "There is one additive, nullable column and a one-week deadline. Alembic would add a dependency, a workflow and operator steps. Without the upgrade, every redirect on the deployed DB would return 503. Failing startup loudly is better than serving 503s.",
   "alternatives": [
    "Alembic migrations (out of scope)",
    "Documented manual ALTER only (operator error risk RK-11)",
    "A separate link_expiry table (more joins on the hot path)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "id": "ADR-3",
   "title": "Expiry evaluated in Python on the narrow lookup row, with an injectable clock",
   "decision": "LinkRepository.get_redirect_target selects only id, url, is_active and expires_at. LinkService._check_redirectable(target) raises GoneError() if the link is inactive, then GoneError(LINK_EXPIRED_DETAIL) if expires_at is not None and self._utcnow() >= expires_at. GET and HEAD both go through _resolve_target, which calls _check_redirectable. The clock is LinkService(now=callable|None); _utcnow() calls it, falling back to models.utcnow(), and normalises to naive UTC.",
   "rationale": "This adds no SQL statements (FR-17). The rule is evaluated on every request with no cache (FR-22), and both methods share one helper (RK-14). Deactivation takes precedence. Tests are deterministic.",
   "alternatives": [
    "WHERE expires_at > :now in SQL (cannot distinguish 404, 410-deactivated and 410-expired without a second query)",
    "In-process cache of links (forbidden; breaks immediate deactivation and expiry)"

  },
  {
   "id": "ADR-4",
   "title": "Backward-compatible idempotency hash",
   "decision": "request_hash = sha256(url) when expires_at is None; otherwise sha256(url + '\\n' + canonical UTC instant 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ'). The replay check runs before the future-instant check.",
   "rationale": "Keys stored before the deploy (url-only hashes) keep replaying. The same instant written with different offsets hashes identically. Adding or changing expires_at gives 409. Replays return the stored link even after the expiry has passed, which matches how deactivated links replay.",
   "alternatives": [
    "Always hash a JSON payload (breaks old keys, RK-15)",
    "Ignore expires_at in the hash (silent replay of a different payload)"

  {
   "id": "ADR-5",
   "title": "SQL aggregation with dialect-guarded bucket expressions that use no bound parameters",
   "decision": "Daily and hourly stats use SELECT bucket, COUNT(id) ... WHERE link_id = :id AND created_at >= :start [AND created_at < :end] GROUP BY bucket.\n\nDay bucket:\n- sqlite: func.date(created_at)\n- postgresql (and the fallback): cast(created_at, Date)\n- mysql/mariadb: func.date(created_at)\n\nHour bucket:\n- sqlite: func.strftime(literal_column(\"'%Y-%m-%d %H:00:00'\"), created_at)\n- postgresql (and the fallback): func.date_trunc(literal_column(\"'hour'\"), created_at)\n- mysql/mariadb: func.timestampadd(literal_column('HOUR'), func.hour(created_at), func.date(created_at))\n\nResult values are normalised in Python (str -> date/datetime).    "rationale": "Memory is O(days) or O(hours) and the query uses the covering (link_id, created_at) index. With no bind parameters inside the bucket expression, the GROUP BY matches the SELECT expression on PostgreSQL. String formats are constants, not SQL formatting.",

    "Stream timestamps with yield_per and bucket in Python (portable but O(clicks) time)",
    "Denormalised hourly counter table (new schema, out of scope)"

   "decision": "health.py adds @router.head('/healthz', include_in_schema=False) and @router.head('/readyz', include_in_schema=False). They return Response(status_code=200) with an empty body. /readyz shares a private _check_database(db) helper with GET.",
